subject: Extract raw copy number using Aroma

messages.author: 66ea21dd30af951a
messages.subject: Extract raw copy number using Aroma
parts:
Hi Henrik,

I want to extract the raw copy number from the cel files. I know
that, for Aorma processed CEL files, I can use
extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs) or extractMatrix(cesN, units=units) for
this purpose.

But we also want to extract the raw copy numbers from the original
CEL files instead of post-Aroma CELs file. Can we use the above two
functions? Please advise.


Jerry

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Extract raw copy number using Aroma
parts:
Hi Jerry,

can you be more specific what you want to extract? When you say
"post-Aroma CEL file", do you refer to the CEL files holding
chip-effect estimates? Before probe-level summarization, which
outputs chip effects, there is only probe-level intensities. Is that
what you want to extract? What does raw copy number mean to you then
- probe-level log-ratios without utilizing the concept of probesets?

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: Extract raw copy number using Aroma
parts:
Henrik,

After I ran Aroma on one plate of CEL files, I used the method on
"http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/calculating-raw-
total-copy-numbers-manually" to calculate raw copy numbers (CNs) from
chip effect estimates by first "extracting" the chip effects and then
taking the log2 ratios. This method will return a matrix (number probe
by number of subjects). I think this matrix is based on the normalized
CEL files not based on the original CEL files.

What I am wondering is if I could extract a similar matrix for the
plate of subjects, but based on the original CEL files? We would like
to know the effect of normalization on detecting CNVs.

Thanks a lot.

Jianxin

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Extract raw copy number using Aroma
parts:
On Mon, Jul 21, 2008 at 6:06 PM, Jerry <jian...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Henrik,
>
> After I ran Aroma on one plate of CEL files, I used the method on
> "http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/calculating-raw-
> total-copy-numbers-manually" to calculate raw copy numbers (CNs) from
> chip effect estimates by first "extracting" the chip effects and then
> taking the log2 ratios. This method will return a matrix (number probe
> by number of subjects). I think this matrix is based on the normalized
> CEL files not based on the original CEL files.

Note that "probe" is typically referring to the single features/cells
on the Affymetrix arrays. The methods you are referring to return
chip effects/raw CNs for units (the same as SNPs on the 10K-500K
arrays). A unit consists of multiple probes. If you do total copy
number analysis (which I think you do), then each chip effect estimate
is a *summary* of the probes in a unit, that is, there is one chip
effect per unit and not per probe.

>
> What I am wondering is if I could extract a similar matrix for the
> plate of subjects, but based on the original CEL files? We would like
> to know the effect of normalization on detecting CNVs.

I am still not sure what you are asking for. Exactly what do you
refer to when you say "normalization"? There are both probe-level
calibration/normalization steps as well as chip-effect normalization
steps involved in the online vignettes. You can easily skip these,
but for any reasonable analysis I don't see that you should skip the
probe-level summarization step. In aroma.affymetrix, we refer to the
probe-level summarization as the probe-level modeling (PLM). Examples
of steps doing that is the RmaCnPlm, AvgCnPlm etc.

The PLMs does not involve normalization. They only summarize the
probe signals into chip effect estimates. Maybe your question assumed
that the PLM includes normalization?!?

FYI, in our CRMA paper we compared the impact of different
normalization steps (e.g. Figure 3);

H. Bengtsson; R. Irizarry; B. Carvalho; T.P. Speed, Estimation and
assessment of raw copy numbers at the single locus level,
Bioinformatics, 2008. [pmid: 18204055] [doi:
10.1093/bioinformatics/btn016].

Cheers

Henrik
